No conflict found between migration 0026 and the existing 0025 (membership_roles) or 0024 (audit-log) triggers — BEFORE/AFTER ordering cleanly separates the last-owner guard from audit logging, and 0025's cascade-safety no-op correctly engages once 0026's trigger has already removed the parent row. Per user's explicit, deliberate scope decision this run, the 4 HIGH findings from the second run (PQ-UX-007, PQ-PERF-001, PQ-TECH-001, PQ-TECH-002) were accepted as documented technical debt and carried forward unchanged rather than re-verified in depth. Verdict improves from NOT PRODUCTION READY to FUNCTIONAL MVP now that both CRITICALs are closed, but Phase 2 still cannot PASS today: 5 HIGH findings remain open (1 new, 4 deliberately deferred), and the gate's own rule requires zero open HIGH/CRITICAL for PASS.

Fifth same-day Phase 2 run — narrowly scoped closing-out pass on the last-owner/Owner-authorization security family, explicitly NOT a full top-to-bottom re-sweep (that was done exhaustively in rounds 2-4). Read migration 0028's SQL in full and independently verified its trigger logic against edge cases (null/invalid role_id fails safe via FK constraint; dangling/nonexistent membership_id fails closed via is_org_owner(NULL)=false; the two independent BEFORE UPDATE triggers now on kontrolia_auth.memberships fire in trigger-name alphabetical order with no security-relevant interaction, since neither mutates NEW). Independently re-ran live exploit tests for PQ-SEC-006 and PQ-SEC-007 against the running local Supabase sandbox rather than trusting the prior round's own testing at face value: both genuinely, independently confirmed BLOCKED, with the legitimate Owner-grants-Owner and 2-active-owner-suspend cases both re-confirmed still working correctly. Then spent one more deliberate round hunting the exact adjacent-door class the brief named: whether membership_roles.role_id (or its sibling PK column, membership_id) could be changed via UPDATE, sidestepping both the 0025 DELETE-guard and the 0028 INSERT-guard. Found and live-exploited a NEW CRITICAL, PQ-SEC-008: kontrolia_auth.membership_roles has zero trigger on UPDATE at all (confirmed via a live pg_trigger query, not just reading the migrations), so a plain Admin can self-promote to Owner (variant A, reproducing PQ-SEC-006's exact outcome through the door 0028 doesn't cover), directly demote the sole active Owner with no owner-count check (variant B, reproducing the original day-one last-owner-lockout bug with no DELETE involved), or hijack an existing Owner role row by repointing its membership_id to the attacker's own membership (variant C, simultaneously de-roling the victim and escalating the attacker in one statement with zero audit trail). This fully defeats BOTH of today's fixes on this table using the exact rows they were built to protect. Also found a secondary, non-security functional regression while tracing 0028's auth.uid() dependency to its real callers: PQ-TECH-009 (HIGH) — the invitation-accept flow runs under a service-role client with no JWT attached, so is_org_owner() can never pass there, meaning any invitation offering the 'owner' role (still selectable in the shipped invite-role dropdown) now always silently fails its role grant on acceptance, compounded by the accept route never checking that call's error. PQ-TECH-001 spot-checked and reconfirmed unchanged (still HIGH, zero test files under apps/). Verdict remains NOT PRODUCTION READY: security is explicitly NOT fully closed this round (1 new CRITICAL), a materially different and worse outcome than the day's prior trajectory suggested — the round's brief asked this distinction be kept separate from the gate-passable question (which also fails independently, on PQ-TECH-001's untested API routes). Phase 2 does not close today.

Sixth same-day Phase 2 run — narrowly scoped closing-verification pass, explicitly not a full re-sweep. Independently re-ran (not trusted from the round-5 transcript) all three PQ-SEC-008 exploit variants fresh against the live sandbox: all three now correctly blocked by migration 0029, with clear specific errors; the legitimate Owner-promotes-someone UPDATE and the service-role invitation-accept grant both independently re-confirmed still working. PQ-SEC-008 and PQ-TECH-009 both genuinely RESOLVED/VERIFIED this round. Confirmed via grep + code read that migrations 0025/0026/0027's trigger functions never call is_org_owner()/is_org_admin() or current_user at all (they are pure data-invariant counters with no caller-identity check), so they cannot have 0028's original current_user-inside-security-definer bug class; is_org_owner()/is_org_admin() both correctly use auth.uid(), confirmed by reading both function bodies. Confirmed no TRUNCATE grant exists for the authenticated role on any of memberships/membership_roles/roles (live TRUNCATE attempt denied). But directly pursuing the round's second brief item — 'is there any other role/permission table that could achieve equivalent privilege escalation outside memberships/membership_roles entirely' — found and live-exploited a NEW CRITICAL, PQ-SEC-009: kontrolia_auth.roles has zero triggers of any kind, and its own ordinary custom-role RLS policies (migration 0019) never restrict the slug value a role may hold, while every guard added today (0025/0028/0029) and both permission helpers trust roles.slug='owner' as a bare string. A plain org Admin can create/hold an ordinary custom role, then relabel its slug to 'owner' via a single UPDATE on kontrolia_auth.roles — a table none of today's five migrations touch — becoming recognized as Owner with zero involvement of membership_roles/memberships. Live-chained into a full, demonstrated organization takeover: the real Owner's actual role was deleted (migration 0025's last-owner count read 2, real + hijacked-slug fake, and let the delete through), leaving the attacker as the sole recognized Owner with zero audit trail. PQ-TECH-001 re-confirmed unchanged via a fresh file search (zero test files under apps/, no test script in either app's package.json) — genuinely still the only open HIGH item from the testing family, and now not the only thing blocking Phase 2: PQ-SEC-009 (CRITICAL) is. Verdict: NOT PRODUCTION READY. Security is explicitly NOT closed this round — a sixth, more severe door was found, live-demonstrated end-to-end including full org takeover. This is honest, adversarial, in-scope verification work, not a repeat sweep: the finding directly answers the exact question the round's brief posed. If PQ-SEC-009 is fixed and independently re-verified in a future round, PQ-TECH-001 (HIGH, unaddressed since round 1) would become the sole remaining item separating this app from a clean Phase 2 PASS — but that is not today's state, and this round does not claim otherwise.

Seventh same-day Phase 2 run — narrowest scope yet, explicitly security-verification-only, no repeat of the full UX/UI/accessibility/performance/maintainability sweep. Independently re-exploited PQ-SEC-009 fresh against migration 0030 (commit 1549077), not taken on the commit message: (1) direct slug='owner'/'admin'/'member' INSERT attempts, all blocked; (2) the exact round-6 grant-then-rename chain (create custom role -> self-grant via membership_roles -> UPDATE slug to 'owner') repeated live end-to-end, blocked at the rename step with is_org_owner() never reaching TRUE; (3) confirmed the real Owner's JWT roles claim still correctly resolves ['owner']. Read migration 0030's full SQL for correctness: is_org_admin()/is_org_owner() now require r.is_system_role; the JWT hook's roles claim now only includes system-role slugs (repo-wide grep first confirmed no caller checks hasRole() against a custom role's slug, so this changes no legitimate behavior); all five 0025-0029 owner-counting queries updated to also require r.is_system_role; the new prevent_custom_role_reserved_slug BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger correctly exempts is_system_role=true rows (live-confirmed via re-running the real handle_application_enabled app-enablement bootstrap and observing its auto-created 'admin-facturacion' system role still get created without incident) and correctly still allows ordinary custom-role slugs. PQ-SEC-009 genuinely, fully RESOLVED/VERIFIED. One more live-exploit hunt for the same general pattern elsewhere in the schema, as directly instructed: kontrolia_auth.applications.owner_organization_id (tested with a properly org-isolated non-owning admin, not one who happened to also administer the owning org as the first attempt mistakenly did — self-caught and corrected mid-round; both the ownership-reassignment UPDATE and a direct redirect_urls tamper attempt were blocked, UPDATE 0 rows affected, confirmed the row was untouched), kontrolia_auth.platform_admins (raw self-grant INSERT blocked by RLS — the table has only ever had a SELECT policy, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy exists so PostgREST/RLS default-denies by design), and kontrolia_auth.user_permissions (a plain non-admin member's attempt to grant themselves an 'allow' permission override blocked by RLS, confirmed is_org_admin()=false for that user first). All three came back genuinely clean — no new CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM finding. PQ-TECH-001 re-confirmed unchanged (still HIGH, zero test files anywhere under apps/auth-server or apps/admin-panel, no test script in either package.json) — now the sole open finding of any severity across the entire seven-round Phase 2 sequence. Verdict rises to PROFESSIONAL BUT NEEDS POLISH for the security dimension specifically: zero CRITICAL, one HIGH (test coverage, not a vulnerability). See the conversational report for the full seven-round closing verdict, which is intentionally more conservative than this section's own scope.
